BodyShape.description: A loose object's shape: { box: { x, y, z } } with half-extents of 50 to 400 mm in x and y and 50 to 500 mm in z, or { ball: <radius> } with a radius of 50 to 400 mm.

oneOf.description: A box, axis-aligned with the place: its half-extents.
A ball: its radius in millimetres.

Corner.description: A corner on a place's floor, in the place's frame: `x` east and `y` north of its origin (`CORE_CONCEPTS.md` §6.1).

x.description: Millimetres east of the place's origin, within ±100000.

y.description: Millimetres north of the place's origin, within ±100000.

EntityKey.description: An authoring key: the name of a file in people/, places/, items/ or organizations/ without .yaml. 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits, - and _, not starting or ending with - or _.

Floor.description: The walkable floor: an axis-aligned rectangle from its south-west corner `min` to its north-east corner `max`. Its edge is the place's walls.

max.description: The north-east corner; each side at least 620 mm from `min`, room for one person to turn.

Furnishing.description: One furnishing of a place: its key, its kind, the centre of its drawn footprint and the way it faces. Its solids name it by key; a furnishing with no solid cannot be built (`ARC-307` rule 1).

at.description: The centre of its drawn footprint, in the place's frame; inside the rectangle that bounds its own solids, and on the floor.

facing.description: The way its front faces, in millidegrees: `0` north, `90 000` east; `0` to `359 999`.

key.description: The piece's name, unique within its place: 1 to 48 bytes of `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `-` and `.`.

kind.description: What it is, as the author labels it (`table.round`): the same slug grammar. A Presentation Pack draws it by this label.

FurnishingKey.description: The name of a furnishing, unique within its place: `table.east`, `chair.east.1`. It names the piece; it says nothing of what the piece is or looks like.

FurnishingKind.description: What a furnishing is, as the world's author labels it: `table.round`, `chair.painted`. Never what it looks like. Not a closed list: a client that has no binding for `chair.painted` falls back to `chair`, dropping one `.`-segment at a time.

x.description: Half the box's width (east–west), in millimetres: 50 to 400.

y.description: Half the box's depth (south–north), in millimetres: 50 to 400.

z.description: Half the box's height, in millimetres: 50 to 500.

Lies.description: Where an object lies, as authored: a place by key, and a point on its floor.

place.description: The place it lies in: a place key.

x.description: Millimetres east of the place's origin.

y.description: Millimetres north of the place's origin.

Millimetres.description: A length or a coordinate, in whole millimetres (1 m = 1000).

Solid.description: A solid box standing on the floor — a counter, a table, a pillar: its footprint from `min` to `max`, and its height above the floor. Nobody stands inside one or walks through it.

furnishing.description: The furnishing this solid belongs to, if any: the key of one of the place's `furnishings`.

height.description: How high it stands above the floor, in millimetres: 1 to 10000.

max.description: The footprint's north-east corner; the footprint is not empty.

description: A body: in a place file, the walkable floor and the solids standing on it (floor, solids); in an item file, one loose object (shape, at). Never both forms.

at.description: Where an object lies: a place and a point on its floor. Required, with `shape`, in an item's body.

floor.description: A place's walkable floor: an axis-aligned rectangle whose edge is the place's walls. Required in a place's body.

furnishings.description: The named pieces standing on a place's floor that a body can meet — tables, chairs, shelf units: at most 64 (`ARC-307`). Each is named by at least one solid's `furnishing`; a Presentation Pack draws it by its `kind`.

shape.description: An object's shape. Required, with `at`, in an item's body.

solids.description: The solid boxes standing on a place's floor — counters, tables, pillars: at most 64. Nobody stands inside one or walks through it.
